title: Local Law - San Francisco
description: Which layer of government requires the Rent Board report and license (local, not state), then the SF Rent Ordinance, Rent Board rules, licensing, banking and petitions.

sections.title: State, local or federal? Which layer imposes the duty to inform the Rent Board

rows.label: Is the "inform the Rent Board before raising rent" duty a state law or a local law?
rows.value: LOCAL - it is a San Francisco ordinance (Administrative Code Chapter 37, added by Ordinance No. 265-20, effective January 18, 2021). No state statute requires an owner to report a rent increase to the SF Rent Board.
rows.notes: This is the direct answer to the state-vs-local question. Section 37.15 sits in the local Administrative Code, enforced by the SF Rent Board.

rows.label: Then where does the "2023 law" come from?
rows.value: THE LOCAL OPERATIVE DATE, not a state statute. Ordinance 265-20 took effect January 18, 2021. Reporting began July 1, 2022 for buildings with 10 or more units, and March 1, 2023 for condominiums and buildings with 1-9 residential units. Rent Board Rule 13.14 applies to increases effective on or after July 1, 2022, and for condominiums and buildings with fewer than 10 units only to increases effective on or after March 1, 2023.
rows.notes: A two-unit 1940 building is in the 1-9 unit group, so its date is March 1, 2023. The site does not assert that any specific date was 'passed' in 2023 - only that the small-building duty became operative then.

rows.label: What did the actual 2023 California state law do?
rows.value: SB 567 (Chapter 290, Statutes of 2023) amended the statewide Tenant Protection Act: it changed the no-fault just-cause eviction rules and enforcement for the state rent cap (5% plus CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower), and it became operative April 1, 2024. It did not create a duty to report a rent increase to a local rent board.
rows.notes: Stated as a negative finding from the bill text, not as a prohibition.

rows.label: Does the state rent cap set the number for a covered SF unit?
rows.value: NO - by statute and by SF.gov. Civil Code 1947.12(d)(3) excludes housing subject to a local rent control ordinance that restricts annual increases to less than the state formula. SF.gov states AB 1482 does not apply to units already under the SF Rent Ordinance rent-increase limits. The local 1.6% (3/1/26-2/28/27) therefore governs, not the state figure.
rows.notes: The state cap only governs units that are NOT under a stricter local ordinance.

rows.label: Does any federal law require informing the Rent Board or cap this rent?
rows.value: NO federal requirement found. HUD FMRs and SAFMRs are voucher payment standards for the Housing Choice Voucher programme, not limits on private-market rent, and no federal rent-registration duty was located.
rows.notes: Federal cap cell remains blank and flagged (F22) because no official general federal private-rent cap exists to cite.

rows.label: Which obligations still apply on top of the local duty?
rows.value: Three independent layers apply at once: LOCAL - Housing Inventory report, Rent Increase License, 1.6% annual limit, anniversary date, banked increases, 30/90-day notice, Rent Board Fee. STATE - Civil Code 827 notice rules and Civil Code 1942.5 retaliation limits; the AB 1482 cap applies only to units outside local rent control. FEDERAL - fair housing (FHA, 24 CFR 100.500 disparate impact) applies to how tenants are treated, not to the rent amount.
rows.notes: Local, state and federal duties are cumulative. Complying with one does not satisfy another.

rows.label: Is the license application a separate form from the Housing Inventory report?
rows.value: NO - they are the same act. Reporting into the Housing Inventory through the Rent Board Portal generates the license automatically for tenant-occupied units; there is no separate licence application and no charge for it.
rows.notes: The Rent Board Fee is a different, separate payment (FEE page).

rows.label: Does the state rent-registration statute (Civil Code 1947.7) soften the local licence rule?
rows.value: Not established on this record. Section 1947.7(b) shields an owner who is in substantial compliance with an ordinance that "requires the registration of rents", limiting remedies to restitution and filing fees, and section 1947.7(c) restores denied annual adjustments prospectively. San Francisco's ordinance states in Sec. 37.15(d) that the Rent Board shall not operate a rental registry "within the meaning of California Civil Code Sections 1947.7 - 1947.8", so the site does not assert that the shield applies here.
rows.notes: A "what the statute says" versus "what it reaches" distinction, not advice. Published as the open question Q-25 with flag F59. Do not plan an increase on the assumption that 1947.7 rescues an unlicensed notice.

rows.label: What is the legal consequence of the duty being local rather than state?
rows.value: The remedy lives in the local ordinance and Rent Board Rules: under Rule 13.14 an increase purporting to be effective while the landlord is unlicensed renders the entire increase null and void, tested as of the effective date, not the date of service; a tenant may petition the Rent Board at no charge.
rows.notes: State courts enforce state law; the Rent Board enforces the local ordinance. Different forum, different remedy.

rows.label: Coverage cutoff
rows.value: Many units built on/before June 13, 1979 have rent control and eviction protection
rows.notes: Verify exact address in PIM; partial exemptions exist.

rows.label: Annual increase
rows.value: 1.6% once every 12 months on anniversary date
rows.notes: Current rate.

rows.label: Ordinance cap
rows.value: 60% CPI, max 7%
rows.notes: SF Admin Code 37.3.

rows.label: Initial rent
rows.value: No limit on first rent for vacant covered unit
rows.notes: Not a reset for an existing tenancy.

rows.label: License
rows.value: Current Rent Increase License required before annual/banked increase
rows.notes: Unlicensed increase may be null/void.

rows.label: Housing Inventory
rows.value: Annual report by March 1; license auto-generated for non-owner-occupied units
rows.notes: No monetary penalty, but notice unenforceable without license.

rows.label: Banking
rows.value: 24 full months; add percentages; no compounding/prorating; license
rows.notes: Notice must state banked portion.

rows.label: Additional occupants
rows.value: No extra rent merely because new/additional roommate moved in
rows.notes: Even if lease says otherwise.

rows.label: Pending legislation (proposed, not law)
rows.value: File 261020 would cap combined banked plus capital improvement increases at 10% per year; version 1, 'Pending Committee Action' on 2026-11-10
rows.notes: Proposed only - creates no current limit. See Rates page RATE-12 to RATE-18 and flags F46/F47.

rows.label: Petition grounds
rows.value: Capital improvement, O&M, comparable rents, Proposition I, utility, 1.21, bond/water passthroughs
rows.notes: Petition/worksheet before notice.

rows.label: Section 6.14
rows.value: Unlimited increase only when last original occupant vacates plus timely 6.14 notice
rows.notes: 60 days generally reasonable.

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins local view
rows.value: Co-tenants not subject; qualifying post-1995 subtenant/assignee only
rows.notes: Legal advice strongly encouraged.

rows.label: Tenant harassment
rows.value: Bad-faith coercion/discrimination/privacy interference prohibited
rows.notes: Larson footnote conflict flagged.

rows.label: Tenant petition
rows.value: No charge, no time limit, ALJ hearing
rows.notes: 516C and 518 forms.

rows.label: Ordinance text 37.15
rows.value: Owners report under penalty of perjury; condominiums and units in buildings under 10 units report from March 1, 2023 and annually by March 1; compliant owners receive a license to impose rent increases; otherwise the license is suspended and the tenant is not obligated to pay the increased rent for months during the suspension
rows.notes: Added by Ord. 265-20; not a rental registry under Civil Code 1947.7-1947.8.

rows.label: Rent Board Fee is separate from the license
rows.value: Every residential dwelling unit owner pays a per-unit fee unless exempt: 2026-2027 is $59.00 per dwelling unit, due March 1, 5% late penalty per month to a 15% maximum; a fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting
rows.notes: Two separate obligations; see flag F33.

rows.label: Recovering half the fee
rows.value: If the fee is paid in full, 50% ($29.50 per dwelling unit for 2026-2027) may be recovered from tenants in occupancy as of November 1 of the tax year; penalties may not be recovered
rows.notes: Not a rent increase; identify it separately on any statement.

rows.label: Units built after June 13, 1979
rows.value: Exempt from the rent increase limitations only, if the first Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 13, 1979 and there was no prior residential use; just-cause eviction protection and the Rent Board fee still apply
rows.notes: The owner-supplied 1940 year would fall before the cutoff if confirmed.

rows.label: In-law unit or second structure on the lot
rows.value: A single-family dwelling with a LEGAL in-law unit is a two-unit building and is not exempt. With an ILLEGAL in-law unit it is also a two-unit building and is not exempt UNLESS both units are rented together as a single tenancy. A single-family dwelling is not exempt if another residential structure is on the same lot
rows.notes: Wording corrected 2026-11-08 against the page; two rented units is consistent with coverage (flags F35, F36).

rows.label: 30-day update duty
rows.value: A change in the owner or designated manager name or business contact information must be reported within 30 days
rows.notes: Separate from the annual March 1 update.

rows.label: License scope
rows.value: License rules apply only to rent-controlled units; SF.gov says the license is not required for 6.14/Costa-Hawkins increases or petition-based passthroughs
rows.notes: Those increases have separate rules and remedies.

rows.label: Housing Inventory data is public
rows.value: Submission information is public, including name and business contact details
rows.notes: Privacy consideration before filing.

rows.label: Multiple-year increases
rows.value: Landlords are not required to file a petition to impose multi-year banked increases; add the allowable percentages; no compounding; no rounding up
rows.notes: 30-day notice (35 if mailed).

rows.label: Where to file and check
rows.value: Rent Board Portal account; report inventory; look up license status by address or APN; paper filings by email or office drop-off
rows.notes: Office open 9-4 weekdays; counseling 415-252-4600.
